topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It welcomes the students, introduces the lecture series, and outlines the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cellular, Developmental, and Experimental Concepts of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They describe cancer as a multistep breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture alongside the methods used to study tumor cells.

topics.label: Distinction, Progression, and Nomenclature of Benign and Malignant Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They define the pathological and histological criteria that distinguish benign from malignant neoplasms, including their progression, invasion, and naming conventions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the mechanical, local, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death in patients.

topics.label: Comparative Incidence of Cancer Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the distribution and patterns of tumor incidence across different tissue lineages in humans and across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Modalities of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the clinical principles of early cancer detection and compare the effectiveness and challenges of screening approaches across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of the learning outcomes and housekeeping reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
